fix(palette): draw translucent vars on the palette's own background (rich-palette-y22)

A theme's translucent variable (catppuccin-latte's block-hover-background
#00000019, cyberpunk's alpha accents) is a tint meant for that theme's
background, but once it left the palette the SGR writer composited it over
black and an export over its canvas: a pale hover tint drew as a black cell
in the terminal. The Palette constructor now draws every translucent var
onto the palette's `background`, so every colour a palette hands out is
opaque and the writer, the exporters and the contrast choosers agree.
buildPalette draws its base colours the same way before deriving on-*,
and getThemeBaseColors returns the colours getThemePalette does.

Hand-written translucency ("#ffffff80" in a template) still composites over
the writer's substrate.

fix(pretty): maxString cuts between glyphs and counts glyphs (rich-pretty-2tq) (#234)

* fix(pretty): maxString cuts between glyphs and counts glyphs (rich-pretty-2tq)

A code-unit cut kept half a surrogate pair, which JSON.stringify printed
as a \ud83d escape the value never held, and the dropped count was in
code units. maxString now counts grapheme clusters, the unit cells.ts
already treats as one glyph, so an emoji, flag or ZWJ family is kept or
dropped whole. Rich counts code points; docs/pretty.md says so.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pretty): segment a string once, and only when it is over the cap (rich-pretty-2tq)

Review (high) found every string under maxString was split into clusters
on every probe; a 2M-char value at depth 4 took ~600ms. The code-unit
length check is back as the no-cut shortcut, and the cut form is memoised
per value. The unit is documented at PrettyOptions.maxString and stated as
clusters of the raw value, counted before escaping; flag, toned-hand and
escape cases are tested.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
